content.thinking:
I need to plan out the file structure carefully before writing, figuring out which imports I need from the builder, paint, path, frame, and math modules, and what the default export signature should look like.

I'm designing a red panda standing balanced on a mossy stone, working out proportions and positions: the stone as a scaled sphere about 0.3 high, the panda's body as a capsule roughly 0.35m tall standing on top with legs positioned to touch the stone's surface, and a raised paw plus curved tail for balance.

Now I'm figuring out the tail's curve using a catmull spline arcing up and back, and planning ringed coloring along the tail using stripe segments based on position, shading them through a cel-paint function that alternates dark and light tones.

Then I'm working out overall height proportions — body and head radii, tail height — and realizing the stone needs to be scaled down to look proportional, so I'm adjusting its dimensions and recalculating where the panda's body sits on top of it.

Now I'm defining the panda's chunky body shape using tapered capsules for rump and chest, positioning the legs beneath, and setting up fur coloring with rusty red on the back and darker brown tones on the belly to match red panda coloring.

For the head, I'm planning a wide skull with cheek ruffs made from pointed cones and a separate muzzle sphere, positioning everything proportionally above the body.

For the ears, I'm layering spheres to create the classic red panda look: a larger cream sphere behind for the rim and a rust/dark sphere in front for the inner ear, positioned at an angle on top of the skull.

Now I'm figuring out the face markings—white tear patches over the eyes and cream cheeks—using position-based paint rules on the head surface, with a boundary around y=0.445-0.45 separating the cream muzzle from the rust fur above.

Still placing eye and tear mark decals...

Now adding small cream eyebrow spheres above each eye, then a simple dark mouth stroke from the nose down, and finishing with thin cream whisker rods extending from the muzzle sides.

For fur, I'm designing a tufted triangle card with a grey gradient that can be tinted, scattering around 120 of these across the upper body where the surface normal faces outward enough, using rust-colored tints for variation and adding ruffs on the cheeks.

For cheek ruffs specifically, I only have access to the hit normal field, so I'll filter for side-facing normals on the head to place cream-colored tufts there, keeping the default flow direction for the body cards.

Now I'm working out leg placement, running capsules from shoulder to paw positions with slight offsets for a raised pose.

I'm figuring out the hind leg and paw geometry, computing where dark paw spheres sit on the sloped stone surface by solving the ellipsoid height equation at each paw's x,z position.

Now I'm adding small cream-colored claw cones on each paw, planning to use a reusable helper function to position each paw consistently.

For the hind legs I'm darkening them to dark brown with a smaller radius taper. Then I'm building the tail with a curved spline from the rump upward and outward, defining a tapering radius profile and painting alternating rust and cream rings along its length, finishing with a dark brown tip typical of a red panda's tail.

Now I'm adding scattered fur cards onto the body and tail for texture, then moving to the stone material, painting mossy patches on upward-facing surfaces using noise blended with a mottled stone base color.

I'm also planning extra details around the stone: smaller side rocks, moss mounds, fern leaf cards, tiny flower clusters, and considering a glowing dendro-style sprout motif as a decorative touch near the base.

For the panda itself, I'm adding an ornate gold collar with a tassel and ribbon, built as a closed circular ring swept around the neck using a catmull-rom path positioned between the body and head.

I'll add a small gold tassel hanging below the bell with a rod and tip sphere, plus a couple short ribbon tails trailing from the nape knot. For the elemental dendro touch, I'll add glowing green crystal spikes clustered on the stone rather than relying on actual glow shading, keeping everything flat-colored. I'm aiming for roughly 150 parts total.

I also need to work out the hit detection and frame support for things like the stick and paw claws, make sure the THREE.js imports and helper functions (like a blob/sphere builder and fur-edge paint helper) are typed correctly, and define how body paint transitions along the belly using a normal-based threshold.

I'm deciding to build a palette of toon-shaded color cels and pass pairs of them into the furEdge helper so each surface gets properly shaded edge colors, applying this consistently across body parts. For legs, I'm setting a dark brown cel for the red panda's limbs, keeping the gradient darker than the rust-colored body.

I'm figuring out how to split leg colors by height — using a position-along-axis check so anything above a threshold renders rust-colored fur transitioning to dark brown below, with a slight wave at the boundary. I'm deciding to skip adding a back stripe or saddle marking since real red pandas don't have one, though I consider adding cream brow patches with small stick details. Now I'm writing SVG code for the fur tuft texture...

Computing a closed ring of points around the head for the ribbon, placing them in a circle at a fixed z-height.

I'm adding a few small pebbles near the base of the stone, positioning them around its ellipsoid footprint so they sit touching the floor.

Now I'm placing moss patches as flattened green spheres on top of the stone, computing their height so they rest on the stone's curved surface, with mottled green coloring for a natural look.

I'm also adding small dendro glow spikes sprouting from the stone's side, computing the surface point so the spike base sits flush against the stone and angles outward with a soft green glow color.

I'm also varying the three crystals, adding a tiny gold torus clasp at the ribbon knot for filigree detail, and positioning the ears tilted outward with a slight rotation near the top of the head.

Now I'm placing the eyes and whisker origins relative to the head center, sizing the nose and muzzle so the nose sits just forward of the muzzle front, and adding mouth rods beneath. Finally I'm scattering cream-colored cheek ruff cards on the sides of the head using a normal filter to keep them away from the face front.

Adding brow spots and paws...

Checking paw-sphere bottoms against the stone's curved surface at each foot position to avoid sinking or floating—settling on y=0.2 for front paws and 0.205 for hind paws, adjusting leg endpoints to match before writing the actual geometry code.

For the tail, I'm setting up radius values that taper along its length with rounded caps, then defining a paint function that bands dark and light rust colors depending on position—checking that nested cel/paint calls resolve correctly, and adding a lighter rust shade to the palette. I'm also double-checking that all imported utilities are actually used to avoid lint errors.

Now I'm finalizing the facial features and body edge shading using ink tones, adding a small cream-colored brow stick, and skipping extra decorative details like stone cracks or glowing runes to keep things simple before writing out the final file with its default export and meta info.
